summary:
Impatiens tricaudata is a small flowering herb found only in the mist-shrouded Lukwangule Plateau of Tanzania's Uluguru Mountains. Collected just twice — in 1932 and 1935 — it has never been seen again, despite decades of searching in the same terrain. Whatever quiet beauty it held among the mountain flora, it left almost no trace.

With fewer than fifty individuals presumed to survive, and possibly none at all, this plant sits at the edge of memory. No known threats drove it here — only silence and scarcity. It exists now mostly as two dried specimens in an archive, a species that slipped away before we truly knew it was leaving.
